heroHeadline: US-Iran Draft Deal 'Within 24 Hours': Trump Says Agreement 'Largely Negotiated'; 60-Day Ceasefire Bridge and Hormuz Reopening on Table — Colombia Votes in 7 Days
heroSubtitle: May 24, 2026 — The US-Iran peace process reached its most consequential juncture since the April ceasefire. On May 23, the Washington Times reported exclusively that a draft peace agreement was expected within 24 hours, with senior negotiators — Vice President Vance, Special Envoy Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalifbaf — having approved the draft framework. President Trump publicly confirmed that the deal is 'largely negotiated' and that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen. May 24 is Trump's declared decision point on whether to resume military strikes. The 60-day bridge ceasefire under negotiation would formalize the de facto ceasefire in place since April and open a runway for the substantive nuclear framework talks — covering enrichment duration, stockpile disposition, and sanctions relief sequencing — that have stalled since May. Pakistan's Army Chief General Asim Munir is serving as the key intermediary. In Colombia, with the election 7 days away (May 31), a new poll showed Cepeda at 44.3% — bolstered by right-wing split between De la Espriella and Valencia — but a head-to-head runoff scenario (June 21) remains uncertain, with Valencia leading Cepeda in one poll 44.6%–41.5%. The election outcome will determine whether Colombia's peace architecture — Total Peace, JEP, ELN talks — advances or is dismantled. On Ukraine, Zelensky stated on May 23 that Ukraine is 'waiting for a US signal' on the next peace round, noting Washington's diplomatic bandwidth is consumed by Iran. Lebanon remains on day 8 of its 45-day ceasefire extension; the Pentagon security track opens May 29.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
